description:
FILED s473t3 (Opus triage of the 79 CATALOG-only blessed rows), on main
d9a2aac0.  PRE-EXISTING.  Probe: scratch/s473t3/probes/p13-local-stash.pl.

ROWS BEHIND IT (baselines/fail-baseline.tsv, 2 rows):
  local.t 275 `localised sub via stash`        (perl-tests/local.t:684,693,700)
  local.t 278 `localised sub via stash slice`  (:705,706)

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl):
    package Other; sub f1 { "f1" } sub f2 { "f2" }
    package main;
    no warnings "redefine";
    { local *Other::f1 = sub { "g1" };  print "glob =[", Other::f1(), "]\n"; }
    { local $Other::{"f1"} = sub { "h1" }; print "stash=[", Other::f1(), "]\n"; }
    { local @Other::{qw/f1 f2/} = (sub {"j1"}, sub {"j2"});
      print "slice=[", Other::f1(), "][", Other::f2(), "]\n"; }
  perl: glob =[g1]  stash=[h1]  slice=[j1][j2]
  PCL : glob =[g1]  stash=[f1]  slice=[f1][f2]
  The GLOB spelling is the control -- `local *Pkg::name = sub {...}` works,
  and restores correctly, in both.

MECHANISM: `%Pkg::` is the live stash and a write to `$Pkg::{name}` must
install into the glob of that name.  `docs/not-supported.md` "Live
symbol-table hashes (`%main::`, `%Foo::`) [DEFERRED]" covers READING the
stash; this is the WRITE half, and it is silent -- no announcement, no error,
the call simply keeps the old body.  Both the element and the slice spelling
must go through the same install path the glob assignment already uses.

CATALOG NOTE THIS REPLACES: sweep-bug-catalog.md local.t, "`local
*{$pkg}{method}` (tests 271-278): temporarily replacing a method via stash
slot - not supported."

FAMILY: `docs/not-supported.md` "Live symbol-table hashes" (deferred, read
half).  Filed as a task rather than pointed at that section because a SILENT
no-op on a write is CLAUDE.md rule 12's sin (the announcement), independently
of whether the feature is implemented.
subject: SILENT WRONG (symbol table): assigning a code ref into a STASH SLOT installs nothing -- `local $Other::{"f1"} = sub { "h1" }; f1()` is "h1" in perl and "f1" in PCL, and the stash-SLICE spelling is the same
